objective: Decouple pi-hud from sibling extension internals by consuming the qualified Git and context provider contracts, while preserving widget behavior, configuration, lifecycle generation, caching, rendering, and shutdown semantics.

in: Characterize pi-hud display, configuration, cache, activity/model/context/Git state, lifecycle, and shutdown behavior.
Replace imports resolving into pi-git/src and pi-context/src with stable contracts from initiatives 01 and 02.
Keep HUD orchestration and rendering local while providers own Git collection and context telemetry.
Remove any temporary architecture-boundary allowlist entries and document provider dependencies.
Add a production-source dependency check preventing cross-extension private imports.
out: Reimplementing Git process supervision or context introspection inside pi-hud.
Changing /pi-hud, widget ID pi-hud, display configuration, or user-visible state semantics.
Redesigning the HUD visual layout beyond changes required for compatible provider adaptation.
Implementing provider services owned by initiatives 01 or 02.

constraints: Implementation starts only after 01-pi-git-service-boundary and 02-pi-context-telemetry-boundary expose qualified contracts.
No production pi-hud import may resolve beneath another extension's private src tree.
Provider adapters must preserve cancellation, boundedness, content safety, and lifecycle cleanup.
The dependency checker scans production extension source only so legitimate isolated tests remain possible.
Any temporary exact-file/import allowlist must fail when stale and be removed before completion.

acceptanceCriteria.text: pi-hud has no production import resolving beneath another extension's private src tree.
Git and context values come through stable typed providers without duplicating provider implementation.
/pi-hud, widget ID, configuration, display state, caching, event lifecycle, rendering, and shutdown behavior remain compatible.
An architecture check prevents future sibling private-source imports and reports zero remaining allowlisted violations.
Focused and repository qualification passes with independent review of decoupling and behavior preservation.

assessment.reason: pi-hud spans nine hooks and coordinates several runtime states; changing its provider boundary can regress lifecycle, caching, cancellation, rendering, and compilation independence.
unknowns: Provider contract final shapes are intentionally owned by initiatives 01 and 02.
Some current adapter logic may belong with providers and require an intentional boundary decision after source inspection.

practices.reason: HUD behavior must be frozen before replacing deep imports.

practices.practice: Explicit provider injection and boundary enforcement
practices.reason: Stable providers and an automated rule prevent recurrence of sibling-private coupling.
Events, caches, cancellation, rendering, and shutdown require integrated evidence and independent review.

obligations.text: Characterize HUD snapshots, configuration, cache invalidation, activity/model/context/Git transitions, narrow rendering, disablement, cancellation, and shutdown before migration.
Verify production-source dependency scanning, provider injection, absence of sibling private imports, no duplicated Git/context implementation, and removal of temporary allowlists.
Run HUD, Git, and context focused suites plus typecheck, dependency, performance, command, and full repository gates, then obtain independent review of lifecycle safety and architecture.

work.title: Characterize HUD behavior and provider interactions

testing.approach: Strengthen adapter, state, cache, render, event, cancellation, and shutdown tests before altering imports.
testing.reason: The widget is integration-heavy despite its small surface.

work.title: Migrate HUD to stable Git and context providers

testing.approach: Replace private imports with injected typed providers, enable the production dependency rule, and test both normal and unavailable/degraded providers.
testing.reason: Explicit providers restore extension independence and testability.

work.title: Remove migration allowances and qualify pi-hud

testing.approach: Remove temporary allowances, run integrated gates, review diffs for duplicated ownership, and obtain independent source-bound review.
testing.reason: Completion requires both compatible behavior and a clean enforced boundary.

decisions.text: pi-hud consumes providers but does not own Git collection or context telemetry.
decisions.basis: The architecture review identifies duplicated/deep internal ownership as the core defect.

decisions.text: Boundary enforcement targets production source, not test fixtures.
decisions.basis: Tests may need isolated imports while runtime extension independence remains the enforced invariant.

risks.text: Provider migration subtly changes cache timing or event ordering.
risks.mitigation: Characterize lifecycle and use deterministic adapter tests before switching implementations.

risks.text: A temporary allowlist masks remaining coupling.
risks.mitigation: Use exact stale-detecting entries and make zero allowlisted violations an exit criterion.
Limit HUD adapters to intent/format conversion and review for process or introspection code.
